findings.why_it_matters: A configured drain timeout is lost after any unrelated settings save, which changes how long shutdown waits for in-flight searches.

findings.fix_hint: read settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout at shutdown time, then apply the env override and the >=1.0 clamp
findings.problem: The scheduler still uses the module-level _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT. That constant is read once at import time from the env var only (triggarr/search/scheduler.py:58-81, used at 611-656). Nothing reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout. The field comment says 'Config value is the default; env overrides', but in this state a TOML value is validated and then has no effect. This is a staged change (the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-recovery-counts-config-design.md:175 plans the wiring), so on its own it is not proven to be a defect. pending: confirm the scheduler wiring lands in the same release.
findings.title: New config field has no consumer, so the scheduler still ignores it
findings.why_it_matters: Users who set the value in config get no change in drain behavior.

findings.fix_hint: consider le=3600.0 to match the planned UI ceiling
findings.problem: The model sets ge=1.0 and blocks inf/nan, but it has no `le` bound. A finite value such as 1e9 in the TOML is accepted. docker-compose.yml:24 and README.md:86 say the drain must stay below stop_grace_period (90s). Without that limit, Docker sends SIGKILL in the middle of the drain. The only ceiling is the 3600.0 'form clamp' named in the comment, which does not exist yet and would not apply to TOML edits anyway. This change only tightens validation, so it is capped. pending: confirm whether a model-level ceiling is wanted.
findings.title: No upper bound, so a config value can exceed the Docker stop grace period
findings.why_it_matters: A drain timeout longer than the container grace period means the graceful shutdown is cut off by SIGKILL.

agent_notes: Diff scope: adds one field to GeneralConfig, `shutdown_drain_timeout: float = Field(default=60.0, ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False)`. It has a default, so no existing constructor call or persisted TOML breaks. Twenty-eight files import this module, and none of them needs a change.

Public API and schema: the change only adds to the API. Settings sets only toml_file in model_config, with no env_prefix and no nested delimiter, so there is no surprise env-var binding through pydantic-settings. TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT is still read only by scheduler._read_shutdown_drain_timeout (scheduler.py:58-81).

Persisted config effect: `_settings_to_dict` (routes.py:227) calls `settings.general.model_dump()`. Every save path that serializes the whole Settings (security, instance add/remove, and others) will now write `shutdown_drain_timeout = 60.0` into users' config.toml. That is harmless and round-trips cleanly under ge=1.0 and finite-only.

Tightening classification: the field is new, so ge=1.0 and allow_inf_nan=False reject nothing a previous version accepted. No compatibility regression is possible. The finite-only guard matches the stated intent that an inf value must not leave asyncio.timeout unbounded, and tests/test_config.py:175-197 covers the default, 0, a valid value, inf and nan.

Staged change: no consumer is wired in this diff. The scheduler still uses the import-time module constant (scheduler.py:81, used at 611, 618, 634, 648 and 656). Runtime shutdown behavior is unchanged. The only latent hazard is the form-save reset recorded as impact-1, and that depends on the later wiring.
Performance: none. This is one extra float validated at config load.
Blast radius: minimal. Config model only, with no runtime consumer yet.
Verdict: shippable as-is. Before DEBT-06 is called done, check that the later plan adds the key to save_settings and the settings page context.
